reproduced_bug: A second native Map bound local identity before its durable claim failed, then unconditionally sent MW_CLOSECHAR_ACK during teardown. World accepted the key-only close and deleted a valid character on the first Map. Both a targeted TCP test and two real native Map processes reproduced this before the fix.
contract: WorldPresence (Unannounced/Announced/Retired) is independent of local loading/ready/closing phase and fenced by exact socket identity. Claim failures remain Unannounced. Announced is set before suspending to send ADDCHAR; a retired identity cannot be reannounced.

Map rereads WorldPresence after awaited save/release and sends CLOSECHAR only for Announced identity on a registered World link. World retirement received during a slow final save suppresses its echo.

MW_INVALIDCHAR_REQ has exact 9-byte body (DWORD char/key, BYTE release-main) and sends empty CS_INVALIDCHAR_ACK before closing. MW_DELCHAR_REQ has exact 10-byte body (DWORD char/key, BYTE logout/save) and closes without inventing a client ACK. MW_CLOSECHAR_REQ has exact 8-byte body and sends empty CS_SHUTDOWN_ACK before closing. Truncation/trailing data/nonboolean flags/wrong keys have no effect.

World-originated rejection/retirement marks Retired while preserving local phase: a locally Ready primary still follows existing atomic save/release. DELCHAR save=0 cannot discard a dirty native primary; this and no close-all echo on every World retirement are explicit modern policies. Successful replica teardown will require its own role-specific release path.

World CLOSECHAR requires matching key, nonzero typed Map ID 0x0400|sid, exact currently registered peer, and an accepted valid connection for that character. Pending/unaccepted/stale peers receive original DELCHAR(logout=1,save=0) without evicting the primary. This strengthens the legacy key-only lookup; accepted secondary close-all remains possible.

Client field widths/opcodes are unchanged. A local admission error after a premature World success still notifies World; a genuine World rejection suppresses echo. Failed persistence retains dirty snapshot/reservation as before.
